 MG Road, Bangalore - 01

JUDGMENT Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

Dorairaj .P vs Chennappa on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63883163/
1

2. Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner no.1 is the husband and petitioner No.2 is the mother of late Radha W/o Dorairaj.

3. That on 08.11.2022 at about 08.30 AM., the deceased Radha w/o petitioner No.1 was traveling in Appe auto rickshaw bearing reg No.KA-08-7109 as a passenger there in along with the other passengers, from Chikka Thirupathi towards Sarjapura main road, near Beglur Anjaneyaswamy temple, the driver of the said auto rickshaw drove it, with high speed, rash and negligent manner and lost his control over the said vehicle and made the vehicle to fall in a trench/stream and there by caused accident.
In the said accident Radha has sustained grievous injuries.
She was shifted to Jayadeva Hospital, wherein the doctor of the said hospital declared that she was already dead.
Later postmortem was conducted at Govt Hospital, Hosakote.
The petitioners have performed funeral and obsequies as per their customs at their native place and have spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- for the same.

4. Petitioners alleged that deceased Radha was 34 yeas of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy and she was working as coolie and she was earning Rs.30,000/- per month and she was one of the earning member for their family.
They stated that the alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the autorickshaw bearing No.KA-08-7109.
The Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.109/2022.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurer, accordingly they are jointly liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.

5. After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondents, respondent No.1 has not chosen to appear before this court and he placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement by denying the entire petition in toto and contended that the insured has violated the policy terms and conditions and the driver of the said vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and insured has allowed the driver of this vehicle to drive the same willfully intentionally and consciously, inasmuch insured is liable to pay the compensation and prays this tribunal to dismiss the petition.
6. In order to prove the case, Petitioner No.1 examined himself as PW-1, produced and marked 10 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 10 and he is fully cross examined.
7. Respondent No.2 examined himself as RW-1 produced and marked 2 documents as Ex.R1 and 2 and he is fully cross examined.
8. I have heard the arguments from the counsel appearing for the petitioners and respondent No.2 is permitted to file the written arguments and he has failed to file the written arguments.

Dorairaj .P vs Chennappa on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63883163/
2 9.

On the basis of pleadings my learned predecessor in office has framed the following:
POINTS 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Radha died in the accident that occurred on 08.11.2022 at about 08.30 AM., the deceased Radha was traveling in autorickshaw bearing No.KA-08-7109 on NH-648, near Beglur Anjaneyaswamy temple cross, from Chikka Thirupathi towards Sarjapura, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of the aforesaid vehicle drove it, in rash and negligent manner and zigzag manner and lost control and fell into a ditch and was turtled.
Due to the accident the deceased Radha has sustained grievous injuries and died on the hospital?

2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. What order or award?
Point No.3:

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 11. Points No.1 & 2 :- I have taken both the issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and husband of the deceased Radha, has reiterated the petition averments in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
12. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-08-7109.

In order to prove the actionable negligence,
Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint, mahazar, Inquest report, IMV report, PM reports and final report which are at Ex.P1 to 7 and adhaar card is at Ex.P.10.
13.

On perusal of the aforesaid documents it is evident that Radha was died in the motor vehicle road accident caused by the negligent act of driver of auto rickshaw that is Babu S. S/o Srinivasa,
who was the drive of the said offending vehicle.
Further R1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and he insured his vehicle with R2.
Evidently respondent no.2 has failed to prove his defence as taken in his written statement accordingly it can not be accepted.
14. In the cross examination of PW-1, he clearly deposed that his wife was working as coolie and she was drawing monthly salary of Rs.30,000/-.

But he has not documents to substantiate the same,
Dorairaj .P vs Chennappa on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63883163/
3
accordingly the notional income of Rs.15,500/- has to be considered as the accident occurred in the year 2022.
15. Further more as per the entry in Aadhar card of the deceased radha which is Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1993.
Accordingly the age of the decease as on the date of the accident was 29 years and multiplier 17 is applicable.
16. Deceased was self employee/coolie and she was below 40 years of age, accordingly 40% should be added towards her monthly income for future prospectus.
Deceased was married and she has left behind 2 dependents accordingly 1/3rd should be deducted from her monthly income towards her personal expenses.

17. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1

Monthly income Rs. 15,500/-
Add: 40% of income future prospectus Rs. 6,200/-
 Rs. 21,700/-
2 Less; 1/3 for personal living expenses Rs. 7,233/-
4 Monthly income Rs. 14,467/-
 Rs.14467 (income)X 12 (month) X 17 Rs.29,51,268/-
 (Multiplier )
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.29,51,268/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.

Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.
20. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.

In this petition, the petitioners are the wife,
minor children and parents of the deceased, accordingly they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.40,000X2 = Rs.80,000/- as compensation under this head.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

Dorairaj .P vs Chennappa on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63883163/
4 21.
In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl No .
Compensation under the Head Amount 1 Loss of dependency Rs.29,51,268/-

2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3 Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 80,000/-
[S In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.30,61,268/-.
22. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
23. Liability:

As per the police records the accident took place due the sole rash and negligent driving of the driver (that is Babu S/o. Srinivas) auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-08-7109 which belongs to Respondent no.1.
It is not disputed that the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said Auto rickshaw.
ExP.9 is the reply given by the insured to the police for the notice issued U/s.133 of IMV act.
Where in the insured has admitted that the driver of his vehicle has no valid diving license as on the date of accident.
As per IMV report, there was no mechanical defects in the said offending vehicle.
Further as per Ex.D1 the policy of the offending vehicle is valid and admittedly it is a Comprehensive policy and the petitioner is a third party to the said policy.

Accordingly insurer has successfully plead and proved the fact that the respondent no.1 has violated/ breach the policy condition that is he knowingly and consciously handed over the offending vehicle and permitted/allowed the driver to drive the same with out valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

Add to it considering the facts and attending circumstance, the clear breach of the policy condition that is allowing his driver to drive the auto with out driving licence, is the fundamental cause for the accident.

The policy for the said auto is valid and Comprehensive policy which is in force as on the date of the accident, such being the case the liability to pay the compensation amount can be attached to the insurer that is respondent No.2,
by adopting the concept of pay and recovery, with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle that is respondent No.1 as per the dictum laid down in National Insurance company ltd

. 
V/s Swaran sing and others - AIR 2004 SC 1531, and also in Papu and others V/s. Vinod kumar lamba and another and also as per Shamanna Vs the Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company- AIR 2018 SC 3726.

5
Accordingly respondent no.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.

Accordingly I am answering Point no.1 in the affirmative and Point no.2, in partly affirmative,
24.
Point No.3;

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid points, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.

Petitioners are entitled for  compensation amount of Rs.30,61,268/-
with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
After depositing the compensation amount with interest respondent No.2 is at liberty to recover the same from the respondent No.1
Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 60%,
petitioner No.2 is entitled for 40% in the total compensation amount with interest.
After depositing the compensation are permitted to withdraw 60% of their share, and balance 40% of their share shall be deposited in nationalized bank for a period of three years.
Issue intimation to the banker not to allow the petitioners to create encumbrance on the deposited amount and not to permit them for premature withdrawal of the deposit amount.

Petitioners have to comply the mandate of of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020,
while withdrawing their respective share of compensation amount with interest.
Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed off.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer then corrected by me and pronounced in open court on this the 15th day of February 2024)
(P. SHIVARAJ) Vth Addl. S.C.Judge & 24th ACMM SCCH-20, Mayohall Unit, Bangalore A N N E X U R E:
